q: Book-value weights taken from the balance sheet are considered unsatisfactory for computing the weighted average cost of capital of an enterprise, chiefly because they represent:

options.B: Amounts that are always larger than the market values of the same sources
options.C: Only the equity capital of the enterprise and none of its debt
options.D: Figures that the auditors of the enterprise have not certified

q: A debenture pays interest of Rs 96 a year and is quoted in the market at a current yield of 8%. The market price of the debenture is:

options.A: Rs 960

In a discounted cash flow appraisal, the interest payable on the capital locked up during the construction period of a work is not also added to the cost of the work as a separate item, because:

options.A: No interest is payable by an enterprise during the construction period of a work

options.A: 6 times

options.C: 5.14 times
options.D: 7.2 times

q: Where the projects competing for a limited capital budget are indivisible, that is, each must be taken as a whole or not at all, ranking them by their profitability index and taking them in that order may fail to give the best result, because:

options.A: That order may leave a part of the budget unusable by the next project in the ranking, whereas a different combination of whole projects, using the budget more fully, may yield a higher total net present value

options.A: The debt-equity ratio of an enterprise is of no use at all

options.A: 4.50 times

Under Accounting Standard 3 (AS-3), where an enterprise holds cash and cash equivalent balances which are not available for use by the group, for example the balances held by a subsidiary in a country which imposes exchange restrictions, the correct course for the enterprise is to:

options.A: Exclude those balances altogether from the opening and closing balances shown in the cash flow statement, without saying anything about them
options.B: Show those balances as a cash inflow from financing activities
options.C: Disclose the amount of such balances, together with a commentary by the management, in connection with the cash flow statement
options.D: Transfer those balances to the investing activities section of the statement

q: The proprietor of a business introduces into the business his personal machinery worth Rs 2,00,000, as additional capital. In the fund flow statement of the business, this transaction:

options.A: Is shown as a source of funds of Rs 2,00,000
options.B: Is shown as an application of funds of Rs 2,00,000
options.C: Increases the working capital of the business by Rs 2,00,000
options.D: Causes no flow of funds, because it affects only a non-current asset on the one side and the proprietor's capital, a non-current item, on the other

q: Where the operations of an enterprise in a year result in funds being lost in operations, instead of funds being generated by them, the amount of the funds so lost is dealt with in the fund flow statement by:

options.A: Showing it on the applications (uses) side of the statement, as funds consumed by the operations of the year
options.B: Showing it as a source of funds with a minus sign in the profit and loss account
options.C: Omitting it from the statement altogether, since a loss cannot be shown in a fund flow statement
options.D: Adding it to the net increase in working capital for the year

q: In a cash flow statement prepared by the indirect method, an increase during the year in the advances received from customers, shown as income received in advance, is added to the operating profit before working-capital changes mainly because:

options.A: Advances received from customers are a non-operating income of the enterprise
options.B: Cash has actually been received during the year in excess of the revenue recognised in the profit, so that the cash generated from operations is higher than the accrual profit to that extent
options.C: Such advances are used for purchasing fixed assets for the customers
options.D: Such advances are in the nature of long-term borrowings by the enterprise

q: A manufacturing enterprise regularly sells, for cash, the scrap and waste material arising in its production process, the proceeds being credited in its profit and loss account as an operating receipt. In its cash flow statement under Accounting Standard 3 (AS-3), these receipts are classified as cash flows from:

options.A: Investing activities, because scrap arises from the fixed assets of the enterprise
options.B: Financing activities, because the receipts reduce its need to borrow
options.C: Operating activities, because they arise from, and are incidental to, the principal revenue-producing activities of the enterprise
options.D: No activity at all, the receipts being simply deducted from the cost of materials purchased

q: A non-banking finance company issues debentures and raises long-term borrowings in order to obtain funds for its lending business. In its cash flow statement under Accounting Standard 3 (AS-3), the cash so received is classified as a cash flow from:

options.A: Financing activities, because activities which change the size and composition of an enterprise's capital and borrowings are financing activities for every enterprise, including a financial enterprise
options.B: Operating activities, because borrowing is the raw material of the company's lending business
options.C: Investing activities, because the money raised will be invested in loans to customers
options.D: No activity at all, because a finance company is not required to show its borrowings in the cash flow statement

q: An enterprise repays in cash a short-term bank borrowing which formed part of its current liabilities. In its fund flow statement, this repayment is:

options.A: Shown as an application of funds, because cash has gone out of the business
options.B: Not shown as an application of funds, because both the cash repaid and the borrowing repaid are current items, and the repayment leaves the net working capital of the enterprise unchanged
options.C: Shown as a source of funds, because a liability of the enterprise has been reduced
options.D: Deducted from the funds from operations of the year

q: For the output actually achieved, the standard gang composition allows 60 hours of skilled labour at Rs 200 per hour and 40 hours of unskilled labour at Rs 100 per hour. The gang actually worked 50 skilled hours and 50 unskilled hours. The labour gang (mix) variance for the period is:

options.C: Rs 1,000 Adverse
options.D: Rs 3,000 Favourable
